numerical_calibration.reason: Approved for riparian design and planning only. The source widths and analysis extents do not establish a shared relationship between site distance to water and buffer establishment.

retained_source_profiles.source_lineage: Zhao et al. selected the mapping window; Lin et al. (2004) and Maillarda and Pinheiro Santos (2008) are cited for service-specific width evidence.
retained_source_profiles.applicability: Liuxihe River basin, Guangdong, China. Nutrient export and buffer condition inform restoration priority.
retained_source_profiles.locator: PDF p. 4, riparian buffer delineation; decision support presented on PDF p. 1.
retained_source_profiles.source_quote: In this study, we set a maximum buffer width of 210 m (distance of 7 pixels, Fig. 3) because a buffer width wider than 200 m was necessary to achieve ideal efﬁciency in some cases (Lin et al., 2004; Maillarda and Pinheiro Santos, 2008).

published_profile.role: Analysis window for spatial prioritisation of riparian restoration
published_profile.interpretation: The authors selected a maximum analysis extent around the channel for mapping restoration priorities. The cited buffer efficiency evidence motivates the window; sites outside were unevaluated.

retained_source_profiles.disposition: Keep the seven-pixel restoration-priority window as the chosen analysis extent.

retained_source_profiles.source_lineage: Dala-Corte et al., fish and aquatic-invertebrate analyses across Brazilian biomes.
retained_source_profiles.applicability: Study concerned streams up to 10 m wide and used 30 m vegetation data. Recommended reserve width does not prescribe a minimum distance from water for establishing vegetation.
retained_source_profiles.locator: PDF p. 9, discussion §4.2, reserve retention and spatial-resolution caveat.
retained_source_profiles.source_quote: Therefore, maintaining 50 m of ripar-ian reserves on each side of the stream channel (resulting in a 100-m wide strip in total) would most effectively avoid crossing thresholds of aquatic biodiversity loss in Brazil.

published_profile.role: Riparian reserve retention for aquatic biodiversity in Brazilian small streams
published_profile.interpretation: Retain native vegetation on each bank. Wider reserves can benefit additional taxa. The authors used fixed analysis buffers and explicitly qualify the precision of the minimum width and shape.

retained_source_profiles.disposition: Keep the native reserve recommendation per bank, the two-bank total, small-stream scope and precision caveat for aquatic biodiversity.

retained_source_profiles.source_lineage: Brazilian Native Vegetation Protection Law (Brasil, 2012), partially adopted by the authors. The paper cites FAO and Welsch (1991) for a 30 m water-quality recommendation.
retained_source_profiles.applicability: Study geometry and cited historical design guidance only. Application of a current legal mask requires the relevant law and jurisdiction.
retained_source_profiles.locator: PDF p. 2, methods: selection of the riparian zone.
retained_source_profiles.source_quote: We adopted the Permanent Preservation Area (PPA) that is deﬁned by the Native Vegetation Protection Law of Brazil (Brasil, 2012) as a riparian zone. We have adopted partially the law and used a 30 m-buﬀer along the river network and a 50 m buﬀer around springs. We did not consider special cases of the law that allow reducing the PPA to only 5 m. FAO recommendation for riparian zone to water quality protection is also 30 m, as well as proposed by Welsch (1991).

published_profile.role: Land-cover analysis zones for assessing water quality
published_profile.interpretation: The study delineated buffers along rivers and around springs. Reduced-width cases in the cited law were excluded from its analysis. The planning profile conveys the study geometry and its historical legal context.

retained_source_profiles.disposition: Retain river and spring analysis zones with their Brazilian regulatory context and the stated reduced-width exceptions.

numerical_calibration.source_count_basis: Three source publications documenting design or planning. No graded response or source weight is inferred.

justification: Approved for riparian design and planning only. The source widths and analysis extents do not establish a shared relationship between site distance to water and buffer establishment. Retained approved calibration hold; no new numeric synthesis or approval.
